nodes.summary: A process with measurable coordinates is adapted to its natural filtration.
nodes.title: Processes with measurable coordinates are adapted to their natural filtration

nodes.summary: For a pre-Brownian motion with measurable coordinates, each increment `B t - B s` (`s ≤ t`) is independent of the natural filtration at time `s` (a consequence of `IsPreBrownianReal.indepFun_shift`, the weak Markov property).
nodes.title: Increments are independent of the past

nodes.summary: For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past, and a measurable weight `φ` bounded by `C`, `E[(∑_{k < n} φ(B_{t_k}) ((ΔB_k)² - Δt))²] ≤ 2 C² t² / n` on the uniform partition `t_k = t k / n` (`n ≥ 1`).
nodes.title: Second moment of the weighted quadratic-variation error

nodes.summary: Quadratic variation of Brownian motion, `[B]_t = t`: along the uniform partitions of `[0, t]`, `∑_{k < n} (B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))² → t` in `L²(P)`, for every pre-Brownian motion `B` (no filtration and no measurability of the coordinates is assumed; Øksendal 2003, Exercise 2.17; Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Theorem 1.5.8 treats continuous square-integrable martingales in probability).
nodes.title: Quadratic variation of Brownian motion

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of `integral_weightedQVError_sq_le`, `∑_{k < n} φ(B_{t_k}) ((ΔB_k)² - Δt) → 0` in `L²(P)`.
nodes.title: Weighted quadratic variation of Brownian motion

nodes.summary: Along the uniform partitions of `[0, t]`, `∑_{k < n} (B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))² → t` in probability.
nodes.title: Quadratic variation of Brownian motion in probability

nodes.summary: The weighted quadratic-variation error along the uniform partition of `[0, t]` into `n` cells: `∑_{k < n} φ(B (t k / n)) ((B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))² - t / n)`.
nodes.title: Weighted quadratic-variation error of Brownian motion

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
